thread:
incident-bot: Pager: High-severity - PrivateLink EU-C (AZ-C) - intermittent DNS rewrite + path flap causing 502/503s for customer traffic. Trigger: 2xx->5xx spike from health checks. Paging oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: ack. looking. any customers naming?

customer-ops: ACME is reporting API timeouts from eu-west instances, started ~07:02 UTC. They see retries and cross-region failovers.

alex.s: I'm on it. pulling up metrics. seeing a sharp TTL rewrite on privatelink-dns in az-c around 07:01-07:06. Also BGP withdraws between az-c and az-d for the PL peering.

nora: can you run a quick dig against the private DNS from a host in az-c?

alex.s: ```
# onbastion-azc
dig +short internal.acme.service.privatelink.local @10.2.1.10
# result rotated between 10.2.3.5 and NXDOMAIN during window
```

jamie: netops, any control-plane changes or route-reflector churn in the window?

netops: we saw flaps on the peering sessions for the privatelink VRF. BFD flapped a few times, then routes got re-advertised with different next-hops causing asymmetric path selection. Not seeing planned maintenance.

oncall-sre: ok, priority: stop customer impact, stabilize routing. Quick mitigation options: 1) pin ACME route to stable AZ (force next-hop), 2) announce static host routes from az-d to absorb traffic, 3) fail traffic to secondary PrivateLink endpoint in eu-north temporarily. Thoughts?

nora: ACME uses rated throughput to az-c primarily. Failover would increase latency but better than 5xx. Do we have capacity in eu-north?

infra-bot: Capacity check: eu-north has ~20% spare reserved capacity for dedicated private endpoints for that SKU.

alex.s: I'll test a controlled routing override for a small subset (canary CIDR) to eu-north endpoint and monitor health.

jamie: also check DNS behavior — looks like our PrivateLink DNS proxy is intermittently rewriting responses with stale TTLs. Could be a cache invalidation bug + race with route changes.

netops: pulling BGP logs now. see rapid updates from provider peering 203.0.113.0/30 -> different AS_PATHs. Might be upstream multipath oscillation. I'm opening a support ticket with the transit provider.

oncall-sre: run the canary. alex.s, when you've started, paste the curl check and health counts.

alex.s: starting canary now -> will announce a /28 override from az-c but prefer eu-north next-hop.

alex.s: health checks: ```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://internal.acme.service/health
# before: 502
# during canary: 200
```

customer-ops: ACME sees a drop in errors now, their dashboard shows 95% success for the canaried subset. Thanks.

netops: transit provider acknowledged oscillation; they have an engineer assigned. Proposed immediate mitigation: suppress one of the multipath links for the apriority to stop route churn. Asking for go from eng.

ops-shift: recommend suppressing the less preferred transit link for 10m to observe stability. SLA impact minimal vs continuing errors.

oncall-sre: +1. Jamme/nora coordinate suppression and keep canary running. Post here when netops confirms BGP stable.

netops: suppressed transit-secondary link at 07:28 UTC. Observing no further BFD flaps. Route table stabilized within 45s.

alex.s: canary health steady. rolling override removal in 5m and will let routing converge back.

jamie: note: DNS proxy still showed a bad TTL rewrite around 07:35 for a handful of records — filing an infra bug. Might be related to cache invalidation when routes change.

infra-bot: created ticket INFRA-2247: PrivateLink DNS cache invalidation race - attaching dig traces and logs.

oncall-sre: summary for now: customer impact mitigated by canary and transit suppression. Root cause likely upstream multipath oscillation exposing a bug in our DNS caching layer that caused short-lived NXDOMAIN/old-nexthop replies. Open actions: netops follow provider ticket to fix multipath, infra team debug DNS cache invalidation (INFRA-2247), runbook update to include canary override playbook, customer postmortem prep.

customer-ops: ACME acknowledged mitigation, asked for ETA on full fix and a timeline for postmortem. Please include whether any customer data was retried/lost.

alex.s: no evidence of data loss; just transient errors and retries. We'll include detailed request traces for ACME in the postmortem.

oncall-sre: handing off to ops-shift for overnight monitoring at 08:00 UTC. If transit provider or DNS bug reproduces, page the on-call immediately and tag netops/infra.

ops-shift: acked and monitoring. I'll keep the canary running for 2 hours and escalate if error rate rises >1%.

incident-bot: Incident updated -> severity lowered to P2; start time 3740012345, mitigated 3740014200, assigned INFRA-2247 and provider ticket PROV-9931. Handoff: ops-shift.

oncall-sre: closing thread now; will attach log bundle and timeline to the incident ticket. Good job team. :thumbsup:
